title: Choppauhshapaugausuck
summary: Choppauhshapaugausuck names the Montauk locality connected with the ditch or outlet of Great Pond on the south, the place from which Ditch Plain takes its English name.
address_label: Ditch Plain / south outlet of Lake Montauk, Montauk, NY (approximate)
why_this_matters: Choppauhshapaugausuck preserves a Montauk placename tied to the outlet where water from Great Pond, now Lake Montauk, opened near Ditch Plain. Its interpretation connects hydrology, movement, and boundary-making. The exact historic outlet cannot be traced confidently across today's altered landscape.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Choppauhshapaugausuck and Chop-pauhshapaugausiick. The name is interpreted as a place of separation where the brook opens out, connecting it with the outlet or small stream flowing from the pond.

Why Place Names Matter

“As highly visible cultural symbols, place names help us collectively navigate and give meaning to our world.”

— Grace Wu, The Living Legacy of Names (2022), UC Santa Barbara news article, quoted comment, paragraph 3
whereintheworld_content: Choppauhshapaugausuck connects Ditch Plain with Montaukett boundary language and the changing wetland and pond-outlet landscape. Available evidence does not establish the precise historic outlet or boundary line.
